body: Pilotwings 64 is Nintendo and Paradigm Simulation's Nintendo 64 flying game, released alongside the console in Japan. Six pilots attempt licence tests using a hang glider, rocket belt and gyrocopter, with additional activities unlocked through progress. Islands contain landmarks, targets and routes that look inviting from above. The immediate objective may be a sequence of rings or a careful landing, but the scenery also encourages the player to look around. Learning a machine gives a different way to explore the same small world.

Tests score more than reaching a destination. Time, accuracy, damage and the quality of a landing can all affect the result, making the final approach something to prepare before the target fills the screen. The hang glider uses air currents, the rocket belt can hover and adjust its thrust, and the gyrocopter requires room to take off and land. Each form of flight asks the player to develop another sense of momentum while reading the same landscape for useful reference points.

Good results open further tests and bonus events, while Birdman mode allows freer exploration in a bird suit. A miniature United States supplies recognisable landmarks alongside playful Nintendo details. Dan Hess's score accompanies the different activities, helping establish a calmer character than the console's other major launch adventure. Pilotwings 64 demonstrates three-dimensional space through the pleasure of becoming comfortable inside it: the better the player understands the aircraft, the more attention can be given to the world passing beneath it.
